pr.title: Draw a draft pull request in italic instead of the subtle color
pr.head: a4f2e98364844b27953a72b92f46ca4e17cd4c55

summary: Projector's panel is the band Claude Code draws above the prompt. It lists each pull request the session watches as a row: the number, a state word (reviewing, clean, draft, or ready), the author when someone else wrote it, the title, and notes such as a conflict or the count of open review threads. A click on the header's count collapses the rows to one line of numbers, such as + #12 #14, where each number's color stands in for its row.

The panel marked a draft with the theme's subtle color, on the row's number, on its draft word, and on the collapsed line. On a dark theme that color sits close to the background, so a draft was hard to read. This pull request keeps a draft in the default text color and draws it in italic instead.

• On a row. The number is italic while the pull request is a draft. The state word is draft in italic when no review label applies. A draft that carries reviewing or clean shows that label in its usual orange or green, beside an italic number.
  • On the collapsed line. A draft no longer has a color of its own. Its number takes the color its other state gives, red, yellow, orange, green, or the default, and italic alone says it is a draft. A held draft, one that keeps its clean label while its author builds a change, now reads as an italic green number, as its row shows a green clean.
The Projector review of c261a9d was clean, with one suggestion about a phrase in docs/plugins.md. The next head, a4f2e98, rewrites that phrase, and its incremental review was clean.

groups.title: How the panel draws a draft
groups.kicker: The row and the collapsed line mark a draft with italic, not a color.
intro: Two helpers in hooks/register.tsx decide how a pull request looks. rowState picks the word after a row's number and its style. statusColor picks the color of a number on the collapsed line. The draft flag, pr.isDraft, comes from the watch daemon's GitHub query.

rowState now returns isItalic: true and no color for draft, so its return type makes color optional. statusColor loses its draft branch, which returned subtle ahead of the review labels. Each place that draws a number passes italic={pr.isDraft} to its Text.

files.note: The two style helpers, and the row and collapsed line that draw a number with them.

checks.text: A pull request still loading comes from loadingOf in hooks/github.ts, whose isDraft is false. So statusColor still mutes it with subtle, and no loading number is italic.

With the draft branch gone, a draft reaches the same red, yellow, and label checks as a ready pull request. The changed collapsed-line test shows a draft with threads as yellow, a held draft as green, and a draft with a conflict as red, each italic. claude plugin test . passed it at this head.
A draft that carries a review label gets its word from reviewLabel, which sets no italic. Only the number says it is a draft, which matches the docs.

groups.title: Tests for each row's style
groups.kicker: Both panel tests now record color and italic together.
intro: The row test and the collapsed-line test each mount the panel with a set of pull requests in different states, then read the props of each number and word. Each now records a pair, the color and whether the text is italic, and compares all the pairs at once. A draft that loses its italic, or a ready pull request that gains one, makes the comparison fail.

files.note: The row test and the collapsed-line test, which check color and italic on every number.

checks.text: The row test expects italic on the two drafts' numbers and on the draft word, and on no other row. Its expectation covers both the drafts and the ready rows, so the italic dropped or put on every row fails it.

groups.title: Panel documentation
groups.kicker: The panel section of the plugin docs says how a draft looks.
intro: docs/plugins.md describes the panel's rows and its collapsed line. The change rewrites both descriptions: a draft's number is italic in the default color, the draft word is italic, and the collapsed line no longer lists a muted color for a draft.

files.note: The row and collapsed-line descriptions, rewritten for italic drafts.

checks.text: This sentence says a collapsed number's color says what its row says, from its notes and thread count as well as its state. The section above defines the state as the reviewing, clean, draft, or ready word, and red and yellow come from elsewhere. Checked against statusColor: red comes from a conflict, a change request, or failing checks, and yellow from open threads, as the list below says.
